Author: Anand Pathak
Bench: Anand Pathak
1  IN THE HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH
AT JABALPUR
BEFORE  HON'BLE SHRI JUSTICE ANAND PATHAK  ON THE 16 th OF MAY, 2024  MISC. CRIMINAL CASE No. 17492 of 2024

BETWEEN:-
 ANIL BATTI S/O SHRI SWRAJ BATTI, AGED ABOUT 27  YE A R S , OCCUPATION: LABOURER R/O VILLAGE
CHOURAPATHA P.S. KEOLARI DISTRICT SEONI  (MADHYA PRADESH)

(BY SHRI RAJENDRA YADAV - ADVOCATE)
 AND  THE STATE OF MADHYA PRADESH THROUGH POLICE  S TAT I O N DHANORA DISTRICT SEONI (MADHYA  PRADESH)
 
 (BY SHRI VIVEK LAKHERA - GOVERNMENT ADVOCATE AND SHRI  J.P.SINGROL - ADVOCATE ON BEHALF OF COMPLAINANT)

This application coming on for admission this day, the c  following:
 ORDER

This is the First application under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. on behalf of the applicant in connection with Crime No. 72/2024, registered at Police Station :Dhanora, Distt. Seoni for the offences under Sections 376, 376(1) and 506(part -2) of IPC.
2.

It is the submission of learned counsel for the applicant that applicant is suffering confinement since 09.03.2024 and charge sheet has already been filed, therefore, chance of tampering with evidence/ witnesses is remote.
It is the specific submission of learned counsel for applicant that date of incident is 22.12.2023 whereas, complaint has been made on 08.03.2024, after delay of 75 days.

Statement under Section 164 of Cr.P.C. indicates that both shared emotional relationship for last 3-4 years and a singular incident occurred on 22.12.2023 when in absence of any family member,
Anil Batti vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 16 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/27036032/
1 applicant visited the prosecutrix at midnight and committed offence of rape.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is highly improbable that at such unearthly hours, applicant committed rape, without raising any alarm and that too complaint has been made after 75 days.
Confinement amounts to pre-trial detention.

He undertakes to cooperate in trial, not to be a source of embarrassment and harassment to the prosecutrix in any manner and shall neither move in the vicinity of the prosecutrix nor shall try to contact her in any manner,
Under these grounds, learned counsel prayed for grant of bail to the applicant.
3. Learned counsel for the respondent/State as well as complainant opposed the prayer and prayed for dismissal of application.

4. Heard learned counsel for the parties at length and perused the case diary.
5.

Considering the submissions and the arguments advanced by learned counsel for the parties,
without commenting on the merits of the case, the application is allowed.

It is hereby directed that the applicant shall be released on bail on his furnishing personal bond of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of trial Court.
